title: CHAPTER 2:APPROACHES TO ETHICS
content: 👋 እንኳን ወደ Part 2 የትምህርት ክላሳችን በሰላም መጡ! በዚህ ክፍል ስለ Jeremy Bentham፣ John Stuart Mill፣ Act- and Rule-Utilitarianism እንዲሁም Altruism በስፋትና በጥልቀት እንመራመራለን። በትኩረት ተከታተሉኝ👇 !

title: 2.3.3.2. Jeremy Bentham: Quantity over Quality
content: Core Focus: Bentham’s Quantitative Hedonic Utilitarianism Jeremy Bentham formulated classical utilitarianism around the simple goal of maximizing pleasure and minimizing pain. His theory is strictly quantitative—meaning all pleasures are equal in quality, so we only measure how much pleasure an action produces. 📌 Two Main Principles of Bentham's Utilitarianism: 1. The Consequentialist Principle (Teleological Aspect): • States that the moral rightness or wrongness of an action depends solely on the goodness or badness of its outcome. • Key Takeaway: The end counts, not the means! The end justifies the means. 👉 የድርጊቱ መልካምነት ወይም መጥፎነት የሚለካው ከተግባሩ በሚገኘው የመጨረሻ ውጤት ብቻ ነው። ውጤቱ መልካም እስከሆነ ድረስ የተጠቀምንበት መንገድ ምንም ይሁን ምን ድርጊቱ ትክክል ይባላል! በሌላ አባባል "ውጤቱ መንገድን ያጸድቃል" የሚል መርህ ነው (The end justifies the means)። 2. The Utility Principle (Hedonic Aspect): • States that the only intrinsic good is pleasure/happiness/welfare, and pain is the only intrinsic evil. • An act is right if it brings more overall pleasure than pain; wrong if it creates net pain. 👉 ለሰው ልጅ ብቸኛው ፍጹም በጎ ነገር ደስታ/ሰላም ሲሆን፣ ብቸኛው እኩይ ነገር ደግሞ ሥቃይ/ሕመም ነው። ስለዚህ ማናቸውም ድርጊት ትክክል የሚሆነው ከሥቃይ ይልቅ ከፍተኛ ደስታን ማምጣት ሲችል ብቻ ነው። --- 📊 Bentham's Hedonic Calculus (Measuring Pleasure & Pain): Bentham created a 7-factor mathematical scheme to calculate net happiness before acting: • Intensity: How strong is the pleasure? • Duration: How long does it last? • Certainty: How likely is it to occur? • Nearness (Propinquity): How soon will it happen? • Fruitfulness (Fecundity): Will it lead to more pleasure later? • Purity: How free is it from accompanying pain? • Extent: How many people/sentient beings are affected? 💡 Classic Example: Deciding whether to give a dying millionaire’s money to the Ethiopian Coffee Club or to famine victims. • Ethiopian Coffee Club = ~1,000 hedons (units of pleasure). • Famine Victims = Over 3,000,000 hedons (saving thousands of lives). • Moral Obligation: We are strictly obligated to give the money to the famine victims because it yields massively higher net utility! 👉 ገንዘቡን ለረሃብተኞች መስጠት የብዙ ሰዎችን ሕይወት ስለሚያድንና እጅግ ከፍተኛ የሆነ የደስታ መጠን (3 ሚሊዮን ሄዶንስ) ስለሚፈጥር፣ እንደ ቤንታም የሥነ-ምግባር ሕግ ገንዘቡን ለረሃብተኞች መስጠት ፍጹም የሞራል ግዴታችን ነው። --- ✨ Three Main Attractions of Bentham’s View: 1. Simple: Only one absolute rule to apply: Maximize pleasure, minimize suffering. 2. Commonsensical: Matches our intuition that morality should promote human well-being. 3. Scientific & Impartial: Objective measurement that treats every person equally—regardless of race, gender, status, or religion. 📝 Exam Hint: Watch out for questions asking about Bentham's view on pleasure quality. Bentham believed push-pin is as good as poetry if it creates equal pleasure! Quality distinctions belong to J.S. Mill.

title: 2.3.3.3. John Stuart Mill: Quality over Quantity
content: 🧠 Core Focus: Mill’s Qualitative Eudaimonistic Utilitarianism Critics argued that Bentham's theory reduced human morality to animal desires, calling it a "pig philosophy." John Stuart Mill saved utilitarianism by introducing quality over mere quantity. 📌 Eudaimonistic Utilitarianism & Pleasures: Mill distinguished happiness (eudaimonia) from simple physical gratification. He split pleasure into two distinct levels: 1. Lower (Elementary) Pleasures: • Eating, drinking, sex, resting, and sensory titillation. • Highly gratifying in the short term, but lead to pain or addiction when overindulged. 👉 እነዚህ ዝቅተኛ ደስታዎች አካላዊና የስሜት እርካታዎች (መበላት፣ መጠጣት፣ እረፍት) ሲሆኑ ለአጭር ጊዜ ደስ ያሰኛሉ፤ ነገር ግን ካለ መጠን ከተወሰዱ ለሱስና ለሕመም ይዳርጋሉ። 2. Higher (Refined) Pleasures: • Intellect, high culture, scientific knowledge, creativity, art, and deep friendship. • Long-term, continuous, gradual, and far superior in quality. 👉 እነዚህ ከፍተኛ ደስታዎች የአእምሮ፣ የዕውቀት፣ የጥበብ፣ የፈጠራ እና የእውነተኛ ወዳጅነት ውጤቶች ሲሆኑ ረጅም ጊዜ የሚቆዩና ጥራታቸው እጅግ የላቀ ነው። --- 💬 Mill's Famous Philosophical Quote: > "It is better to be a human being dissatisfied than a pig satisfied; better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied." 👉 ከሚረካ እርያ (pig) የማይረካ ሰው መሆን ይበልጣል፤ ከሚረካ ሞኝ ደግሞ የማይረካ ሶቅራጥስ መሆን ይበልጣል! ምክንያቱም የሰው ልጅ ከፍተኛ የአእምሮ፣ የዕውቀት እና የጥበብ እርካታን የመፈለግና የማሰብ ተፈጥሮ አለው። --- 🎯 Mill's Definition of True Happiness: Happiness is not a continuous state of intense ecstasy, but moments of delight in an existence made of few transitory pains, many diverse pleasures, an active lifestyle, and realistic expectations from life. 👉 ሚል እውነተኛ ደስታ የሚለው የማያቋርጥ የደስታ ስሜትን ሳይሆን፣ ጥቂት ጊዜያዊ ሕመሞች ባሉበት፣ የተለያዩ መልካም ደስታዎችና ንቁ የሕይወት እንቅስቃሴ ባለው ተዚሞታዊ ሕይወት ውስጥ የሚገኝ የደስታ ቅጽበትን ነው። 📝 Exam Hint: Remember the core difference! Bentham = Quantitative (Hedonic Calculus). Mill = Qualitative (Higher vs. Lower Pleasures). If an exam question mentions "Socrates vs. Fool" or "Pig Philosophy," the answer is always J.S. Mill!

title: 2.3.3.4. Act- and Rule-Utilitarianism
content: ⚖️ Core Focus: Comparing Act-Utilitarianism and Rule-Utilitarianism How do we practically apply the principle of utility in daily life? Philosophers divided utilitarianism into two main operational branches: 📌 1. Act-Utilitarianism (Bentham): • Definition: An act is right if and only if it produces as much or more net good as any available alternative at that specific moment. • Major Drawbacks: 1. Calculation Time: We rarely have time to perform complex calculations on the spot before making split-second decisions. 2. Contradicts Intuition: Can justify shocking acts (e.g., lying, framing innocent people) if the math favors it. 👉 አክት-ዩቲሊታሪያኒዝም እያንዳንዱን ድርጊት በወቅቱ በሚያመጣው ውጤት ብቻ ይመዝናል። ነገር ግን ድርጊቶችን በየስከንዱ ለማስላት ጊዜ ማጣታችን እና አንዳንዴ ንጹሐንን መክሰስን የመሰሉ ምግባረ-ብልሹ ነገሮችን ሊደግፍ መቻሉ ትልቅ ድክመቱ ነው። --- 📌 2. Rule-Utilitarianism (Mill): • Definition: An act is right if and only if it conforms to a set of general rules whose universal adoption leads to greater overall social utility. • Why it works: Humans are naturally rule-following creatures. General rules like "Do not lie" or "Keep your promises" act as practical shortcuts that save time and consistently maximize happiness over time. 👉 ሩል-ዩቲሊታሪያኒዝም ደግሞ ማህበረሰቡ ሁልጊዜ ሊከተላቸው የሚገቡ አጠቃላይ ሕጎች (ለምሳሌ፦ "አትዋሽ"፣ "ቃልህን አትጠፍ") ላይ ያተኩራል። እነዚህ ሕጎች በረጅም ጊዜ ሂደት የህብረተሰቡን ደስታ ጨምረው ያስቀጥላሉ። --- 🚃 Interactive Thought Experiment: The Trolley Problem You are driving a runaway trolley car with broken brakes. Five workers are on the track ahead. You can switch to a sidetrack, but there is one worker on it. • What should you do? • Utilitarian Analysis: Switching tracks kills 1 person but saves 5 lives. Net outcome = +4 lives saved. Therefore, switching tracks is the morally required choice to maximize overall utility! 👉 የባቡሩን አቅጣጫ በመቀየር አንድን ሰው መስዋዕት ማድረግ የአምስት ሰዎችን ሕይወት ስለሚያድን (Net +4)፣ በዩቲሊታሪያኒዝም እይታ ትክክለኛውና ብቸኛው የሞራል ውሳኔ ነው! 📝 Exam Hint: Act-Utilitarianism evaluates individual actions case-by-case. Rule-Utilitarianism evaluates general moral rules over long-term outcomes.

title: Strengths of Utilitarianism
content: 🌟 Core Focus: Why Utilitarianism is a Powerful Ethical Framework Utilitarianism remains one of the most widely applied ethical frameworks in law, public policy, and economics due to three major strengths: 📌 1. Single, Universal Absolute Principle: • Offers a clear decision-making guide for every imaginable scenario: Always promote the greatest net utility! 📌 2. Substantive & Human-Centered Core: • Morality is not just about abstract, rigid rules. It focuses on concrete human flourishing and relieving real suffering in the world. 👉 ግብረገብነት በወረቀት ላይ የተፃፈ ደረቅ ሕግን መከተል ብቻ ሳይሆን፣ የሰዎችን እውነተኛ ሥቃይ መቀነስና ደስታን መጨመር እንደሆነ ያምናል። • Kitty Genovese Case: We must intervene or call the police because aiding someone in danger reduces massive disutility. • Dead Millionaire Case: Keeping a promise to give $2 Million to a wealthy sports club is absurd when that money could save hundreds of thousands of famine victims from starvation. 👉 ቃልን ከመጠበቅ ይልቅ በመቶ ሺዎች የሚቆጠሩ ሰዎችን ከረሃብ ማዳን እጅግ የላቀ ጥቅም ስላለው በውጤቱ ላይ ማተኮር አስፈላጊ መሆኑን ያሳያል። --- 📌 3. Solutions for Posterity (Future Generations): • Explains why we must preserve natural resources, protect wildlife, and curb carbon emissions for people who do not yet exist. • Since future generations will experience pleasure and pain, our current moral obligation is to leave them a healthy, viable planet. 👉 የመጪው ትውልድ ደስታና ሥቃይ የሚሰማው በመሆኑ፣ የተፈጥሮ ሀብትን የመጠበቅና የአካባቢ ጥበቃ የማድረግ የሞራል ግዴታ አለብን። 📝 Exam Hint: Contrast Utilitarianism with Ethical Egoism on future generations. Egoists have zero motivation to help posterity (since the unborn cannot benefit them), whereas Utilitarians have a direct duty to maximize future global welfare!

title: Criticisms of Utilitarianism
content: ⚠️ Core Focus: Theoretical Flaws and Standard Objections Despite its attractions, critics point out several deep theoretical and practical flaws in utilitarian thought: 📌 1. Problem with Formulation ("Greatest happiness for the greatest number"): • Two variables ("happiness" vs. "number") can conflict! • The Running Contest Example: A $1,000 prize is offered for running the longest distance in the shortest time. • Abebe: 5 km in 31 minutes • Kelbesa: 7 km in 50 minutes • Obang: 1 km in 6 minutes • Who wins? Abebe ran far, Obang was fast, Kelbesa ran longest. Utilitarianism struggles to prioritize total utility vs. average distribution. 👉 አጠቃላይ የደስታ መጠንን ለመጨመር እንሥራ ወይስ ደስታውን ለብዙ ሰዎች ለማከፋፈል? ሁለቱ ተለዋዋጮች (variables) እርስ በርሳቸው ስለሚጋጩ ውሳኔ መስጠት ያስቸግራል። --- 📌 2. The Comparative Consequences Objection: • Requires superhuman foresight to predict complex long-term consequences far into the indefinite future. 👉 ወደፊት የሚመጣውን ረጅም ጊዜ ውጤት በትክክል ለመተንበይ ከሰው ልጅ አቅም በላይ የሆነ እይታን ይጠይቃል። 📌 3. The Consistency Objection to Rule-Utilitarianism: • Rule-utilitarianism collapses back into act-utilitarianism whenever breaking a rule yields slightly higher hedons (e.g., lying to spare someone's feelings gives 102 hedons vs. 100 for truth). --- 📌 4. The No-Rest Objection: • Demands endless self-sacrifice! Every time you sleep or go to a movie, you could be helping the poor or saving the environment, creating perpetual guilt. 👉 ማንኛውም የምናደርገው እረፍት ወይም መዝናናት ሌሎችን ልንረዳበት የሚችል ሰዓት በመሆኑ ሁልጊዜ የጥፋተኝነት ስሜት እንዲሰማን ያደርጋል። 📌 5. The Publicity & Relativism Objections: • Publicity: Calculating consequences is too complex for everyday people, forcing society to rely on simpler non-utilitarian rules. • Relativism: Endorses different rules based on context (e.g., severe water restrictions in deserts vs. none in water-abundant zones). 📝 Exam Hint: Remember the running contest example! It illustrates the dual-variable conflict between maximizing total pleasure versus spreading it among the maximum number of people.

title: Criticism of the Ends Justifying Immoral Means
content: 🚨 Core Focus: Utilitarianism vs. Basic Rights and Justice The most severe critique of utilitarianism is that it permits committing atrocious, immoral acts if they yield a positive net outcome for the majority. 📌 1. The Lying Objection (W.D. Ross): • Truth has intrinsic value. Utilitarianism treats lying and truth-telling as identical if both produce equal hedons, which violates common moral sense. --- 📌 2. The Justice Objections (Crucial Exam Cases!): • Case A: The Frame-up (Sheriff & The Mob) To stop a massive race riot that will kill dozens, a sheriff frames an innocent homeless man for a crime. Executing him restores peace. • Utilitarian Verdict: Frame the innocent man to save net lives. • Moral Backlash: Violates fundamental human rights and justice! 👉 የብዙ ሰዎችን ሕይወት ለማዳን ሲባል ብቻ ንጹሕ ሰውን በሐሰት ከሶ መግደል የፍትሕንና የሰብአዊ መብትን መርህ ፍጹም የሚጥስ በመሆኑ ትልቅ ነቀፌታ ይቀርብበታል። • Case B: The Transplant Doctor A doctor harvests organs from one healthy patient visiting for a flu shot to save five dying patients needing transplants. • Utilitarian Verdict: Kill 1 to save 5. • Moral Backlash: Terrifying abuse of medical ethics. 👉 አንድን ጤናማ ሰው ገድሎ ህዋሳቱን ለአምስት ታማሚዎች መስጠት 5 ሰዎችን ያድናል፤ ነገር ግን ይህ አስቃቂ የሕክምና ሥነ-ምግባር ጥሰት ነው። • Case C: Torturing the Innocent Child A terrorist is set to detonate a nuclear bomb in NYC. The only way to stop him is torturing his 10-year-old daughter on live TV. • Utilitarian Solution: Rule-utilitarians use remainder rules (maximize utility when rules conflict) to justify torturing the child to save millions. 📝 Exam Hint: Utilitarianism treats justice as a secondary, negotiable rule rather than an absolute principle. Be ready to evaluate these exact scenario questions on exams!

title: The Three-Step Action Formula & Practical Questions
content: 📋 Core Focus: How to Apply Utilitarianism Step-by-Step Utilitarian decision-making follows a simple 3-step action formula: 1. Project Consequences: Identify all available actions (including doing nothing) and project their future consequences. 2. Calculate Utility: Quantify total happiness vs. unhappiness produced for every affected party. 3. Select the Optimum: Pick the action that produces the greatest net happiness for the greatest number of affected beings. --- ❓ Discussion Questions for Students: • Scenario A: A doctor lies to an overly depressed patient about their terminal condition to prevent immediate suicide or severe emotional collapse. • Scenario B: A doctor prescribes harmless placebos or requested antibiotics for mild flu symptoms just to calm an anxious patient. 💡 Key Insight: The frequent occurrence of such white lies in real life suggests that human behavior often naturally defaults to utilitarian thinking—prioritizing immediate beneficial outcomes over strict, unyielding rules! 👉 በእለት ተእለት ሕይወታችን የምንጠቀማቸው ለበጎ የተነገሩ ውሸቶች (white lies) የሰው ልጅ ተፈጥሯዊ አስተሳሰብ ከደረቅ ሕግ ይልቅ ለውጤት አዎንታዊነት (utilitarianism) አድልዎ እንደሚያደርግ ያሳያል። 📝 Exam Hint: Remember Bentham's core slogan: "The greatest happiness of the greatest number." Always apply this slogan when solving step-by-step case problems.

title: 2.3.3.5. Altruism
content: 🤝 Core Focus: Altruism vs. Psychological Egoism Altruism is the ethical view that an action is morally right if its consequences are favorable to everyone except or regardless of the actor. 📌 Key Concepts of Altruism: • Altruists: Individuals who act specifically to increase other people's happiness, even at the cost of personal suffering or decreased personal pleasure. • Psychological Altruism (Joseph Butler): Holds that human beings possess an inherent, instinctive psychological capacity for benevolence and other-centered care. 👉 ሳይኮሎጂካል አልትሩኢዝም እንደሚያምነው የሰው ልጅ በተፈጥሮው ለሌላው የማሰብና የመረዳት አቅምና ፍላጎት አለው። --- 🌊 Case Example: Degu at Lake Tana • Degu, a poor swimmer, jumps into Lake Tana to rescue a drowning child, risking his own life. • Psychological Egoist Claim: Degu did it for fame, guilt avoidance, or personal pride. • Psychological Altruist Counter-Argument: Degu risked his immediate survival purely out of instinctive benevolence for the child. Self-benefit was not his primary motive. 👉 ደጉ ሕይወቱን አደጋ ላይ ጥሎ ህፃኑን ያደነው ለራሱ ጥቅም ወይም ዝና ፈልጎ ሳይሆን ከተፈጥሮ በጎ አድራጊነት የመነጨ ለሌላው የማሰብ ስሜት (altruism) ስላለው ነው። --- ⚖️ Egoistic vs. Altruistic Desires: • Egoistic Desire: Focuses exclusively on perceived benefits to oneself. • Altruistic Desire: Focuses genuinely on benefiting at least someone other than oneself. 📝 Exam Hint: Contrast psychological egoism (all actions are self-motivated) with psychological altruism (some actions are genuinely motivated by instinctive benevolence). ለዛሬው ከዚህ ላይ እናቁምና በቀጣይ (PART 3) DEONTOLOGICAL ETHICS እናያለን። በደህና ቆዩን
